scenario_description:
Objective: Finish the galley inline filter cartridge swap and restore potable sink water before the afternoon resin-tool cleanup.
Emerging Need: The swap has already begun, but the old cartridge is out and the open housing collar will not reseat, leaving the pump isolated and the task unable to continue unaided.
Decision Context: Stored onboard notes supply the filter model, the no-force rule, and the access-clearance route; live messages and dispatch emails establish when help remains feasible.
Consequence: After the dockside routing window closes, the line stays open and tagged off until a later service visit, disrupting cleanup and ordinary galley use.

parameter.title: Galley filter cartridge swap and rinse
parameter.description: Replace the inline cartridge before afternoon resin-tool cleanup; restore pump and flush the galley sink afterward.

parameter.content: I saw the galley cabinet open and the pump switch tagged off while you started the filter swap. Sink towels are on your counter if the housing drips.
Old cartridge is out, but the locking collar will not catch even with hand pressure. I’m leaving the freshwater pump tagged off because the housing is still open.

parameter.subject: Today's potable-water call window
parameter.body: Bluewater has one dockside potable-water opening between 11:15 and noon. Requests with the housing model and marina access contact must be in before 10:30; after that the technician boards the northbound route.

parameter.subject: Northbound route closed
parameter.body: The dockside potable-water slot left without a marina-cleared request. The next standard opening is Friday morning; keep any isolated freshwater assembly tagged off until serviced.
